label: One-way truce
summary: Sets a truce held by the character against the given character, in that direction only.
details: The truce lasts for the time given in years, months or days. With `override = yes` it replaces an existing truce even if the new one is shorter. `result` says how the truce counts from the character's point of view (`victory`, `defeat` or `white_peace`, white peace by default). Give either a casus belli (the war reason that caused it) or a custom `name` for the truce text, not both.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the truce is held against.

fields.name: years / months / days
fields.text: How long the truce lasts.
fields.values: a number or a script value

fields.name: override
fields.text: Whether the new truce replaces an existing one even when it is shorter.

fields.name: result
fields.text: The outcome the truce stands for, seen from the character's side.

fields.name: casus_belli / war
fields.text: The casus belli or war that caused the truce. Cannot be combined with name.

fields.name: name
fields.text: A custom description of the truce, shown in the game.

label: Tyranny
summary: Adds tyranny to the character, or removes it with a negative amount.
details: Vanilla mostly writes a named amount such as `minor_tyranny_gain` or `medium_tyranny_gain`. It can also be a block with `value`, and vanilla once uses `multiply` to scale the amount by a number (the tier of a title).

fields.name: value
fields.text: How much tyranny to add.
fields.values: a number, a script value or a named amount like medium_tyranny_gain

fields.name: multiply
fields.text: Multiplies the amount by this number (block form).
fields.values: a number or a script value

label: House unity
summary: Adds unity to the dynasty house.
details: Runs on a dynasty house. Vanilla also uses loss amounts such as `medium_unity_loss`, so the amount can lower unity. `desc` is a localization key; going by its name and vanilla's keys, it is the text shown for the change. Vanilla always gives all three fields.

fields.name: value
fields.text: How much unity to add.
fields.values: a number, a script value or a named amount like medium_unity_gain

fields.name: character
fields.text: A character tied to the change; the game's documentation does not say more. Vanilla gives the root character, the house head or an actor.

fields.name: desc
fields.text: A localization key describing the change.

label: Claim (unpressed)
summary: Gives the character an unpressed claim on a title.
details: Written as `add_unpressed_claim = <title>`, for example a saved scope or `title:k_burgundy`. The game's documentation does not explain what makes a claim unpressed.

label: Visiting courtier
summary: Makes the given character a guest at the character's court.
details: The character running the effect is the host. Vanilla gives it a saved scope or a link to the guest.

label: Wanderer perk points
summary: Gives the character perk points for the wanderer lifestyle.

label: Wanderer experience
summary: Gives the character experience in the wanderer lifestyle.
details: Vanilla uses plain numbers (100, 250, 500) and named amounts such as `massive_lifestyle_xp`.

label: War chest gold
summary: Adds gold to the character's war chest, a category of the AI's budget.
details: The gold is created from nothing. The war chest has a maximum, and anything over it goes into the short-term budget instead. Written as `add_war_chest_gold = X`.

label: Adopt
summary: Makes the character the parent of the given character.
details: The character running the effect becomes the new parent; the value is the child. Vanilla uses it on a hostage.

label: AI builds a building
summary: Makes the AI character look at which buildings it could build or upgrade in its domain and start one if it can pay.
details: Written as `= yes`; vanilla always writes `yes`.

label: AI hosts activity
summary: Makes the AI character re-evaluate whether it wants to host the given activity type.
details: It ignores the activity's normal AI check interval and cooldown. Vanilla uses it with activity types like `activity_hunt` or `activity_feast`.

label: AI starts best war
summary: Makes the AI character start the highest-scored war from the wars it could start.
details: The AI first filters its possible wars with your `is_valid` block. In it, `root` is the AI character, and the game provides saved scopes such as `scope:target_character`, `scope:target_title`, `scope:casus_belli_type` and `scope:score`. `on_success` runs when a war started, `on_failure` when none did. `multi_target` can start several wars at once (a count and an optional strength limit). `cb` limits the allowed casus belli types, and `first_valid_cb_type = yes` takes the first valid one for speed.

fields.name: cb
fields.text: The casus belli types the war may use.
fields.values: a list of casus belli types

fields.name: is_valid
fields.text: Filter for possible wars; only wars passing it are considered.

fields.name: on_success
fields.text: Effects run after a war was started.

fields.name: on_failure
fields.text: Effects run when no war was found or started.

fields.name: multi_target
fields.text: Start several wars: `count` is how many, `max_accumulative_strength` an optional strength limit for extra targets.

fields.name: first_valid_cb_type
fields.text: Take the first valid casus belli instead of the best one, for speed.

fields.name: recalculate_cb_targets
fields.text: Recompute the AI's casus belli targets instead of using the current data. Only if needed.

label: Allow alliance
summary: Lets the character make an alliance with the given character again after it was broken.
details: The game's documentation speaks of an alliance that was broken before.

label: Allow in scheme
summary: Lets the character join the given scheme as an agent.

label: Fire councillor
summary: Makes the character fire the given character from their council, skipping the usual rule checks.
details: It ignores rules such as the AI's `ai_can_reassign_council_positions`. The `_skip_effects` version is documented as also skipping on_actions, which suggests this one does not.

label: Fire councillor quietly
summary: Makes the character fire the given character from their council without rule checks and without running on_actions.
details: Like `always_fire_councillor`, but the on_actions that normally follow a firing do not run.

label: Apply liege's admin province obligation
summary: Sets the administrative province obligation level in the contract to the level the liege most wants.
details: This is for AI contracts. Written as `= yes`.

label: Apply vassal's admin province obligation
summary: Sets the administrative province obligation level in the contract to the level the vassal most wants.
details: This is for AI contracts. Vanilla does not use it in the input.

label: Apply liege's obligation
summary: Sets the vassal obligation level in the contract to the level the liege most wants.
details: This is for AI contracts. Written as `= yes`.

label: Apply vassal's obligation
summary: Sets the vassal obligation level in the contract to the level the vassal most wants.
details: This is for AI contracts. Written as `= yes`.

label: Appoint court position
summary: Gives a court position in the character's court to the given character.
details: The character running the effect is the ruler whose court it is. The recipient gets the position.

fields.name: recipient
fields.text: The character who receives the position.

fields.name: court_position
fields.text: Which court position to give.

label: Assert if
summary: Raises a debugging error while the game runs when the condition is true.
details: A developer tool for catching situations that should never happen. Vanilla uses it with a message describing what went wrong.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: The condition that triggers the error.

fields.name: text
fields.text: A message printed with the error.

label: Assert on read
summary: Raises a debugging error when the script is read, not while the game runs.
details: The value is `yes`, or a text that is printed with the error.

label: Commander
summary: Makes the given character the commander of the army.
details: Runs on an army. The documented example writes `set_commander`, but the key is `assign_commander`, which is also what vanilla uses.

label: Assign council task
summary: Puts the given character on a council task.
details: `fire_on_actions` is optional in the documented usage; it is not described further.

fields.name: council_task
fields.text: The council task to assign.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The character who takes the task.

fields.name: fire_on_actions
fields.text: Whether the related on_actions are fired.

label: Assign councillor
summary: Puts the given character in a council position of one type, such as chancellor or steward.
details: With `remove_existing_councillor = yes`, whoever holds that position is removed first; the game's documentation adds a note '(not fired)' there, without saying exactly what is not fired. Vanilla uses it with types like `councillor_chancellor` and `councillor_court_chaplain`.

fields.name: type
fields.text: The council position type.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The character who takes the position.

fields.name: fire_on_actions
fields.text: Whether the related on_actions are fired.

fields.name: remove_existing_councillor
fields.text: Remove the current holder first.

label: Auto-assign agents
summary: Fills the scheme with agents who are competent and willing.
details: Runs on a scheme, written as `auto_assign_scheme_agents = yes`.

label: Banish
summary: Banishes the character.
details: Written as `banish = yes`.

label: Battle event
summary: Shows an event line in a battle and in its result summary.
details: Runs on one side of a combat. The key is a localization key; the game adds `_friendly` or `_enemy` to it. When the side is not the player's, the two portraits swap places. Vanilla also sets a `type` (`death`, `wound` or `imprison`).

fields.name: key
fields.text: The text key of the event.

fields.name: left_portrait
fields.text: The character shown on the left.

fields.name: right_portrait
fields.text: The character shown on the right.

fields.name: type
fields.text: Not in the game's documentation; vanilla always sets it.
fields.values: death, wound or imprison (as used by vanilla)

fields.name: target_right
fields.text: Used by vanilla with yes; the game's documentation does not describe it.

label: Become independent
summary: Makes the character an independent ruler, using a title and vassal change prepared earlier.
details: The `change` is a saved title-and-vassal change made before; this effect applies it.

fields.name: change
fields.text: The earlier prepared title and vassal change.

label: Start building holding
summary: Starts construction of a holding of the given type in the province.
details: Written as just the holding type, or as a block. By default a player gets nothing back if they cancel the construction; `refund_cost` sets what they get back.

fields.name: type
fields.text: The holding type to build.
fields.values: a holding type such as castle_holding

fields.name: refund_cost
fields.text: What is refunded if the construction is cancelled, such as `gold = 100`.

label: Break alliance
summary: Ends the character's alliance with the given character.

label: Break betrothal
summary: Ends the betrothal between the character and the given character.
details: Vanilla often passes the link `betrothed`, meaning the character's own betrothed.

label: Cancel great project
summary: Stops the planning or construction of a great project.
details: The project's cancel effects run. There is no refund. Vanilla runs it on the project itself with `= this`.

label: Cancel the journey
summary: Drops the rest of a travel plan, leaves its activities and sends the traveller home.
details: Runs on a travel plan, written as `= yes`.

label: Cancel truce (both)
summary: Ends the character's truce against the given character, and that character's truce against the character.
details: For ending only one direction, see `cancel_truce_one_way`.

label: Cancel truce (one way)
summary: Ends the character's truce against the given character.
details: Only the character's truce against the given character is named; for both directions see `cancel_truce_both_ways`.

label: Change age
summary: Raises or lowers the character's age by the given amount.
details: Age cannot go below 0. This skips birthday on_actions, age-related health and similar things, like the console command.

label: Appointment investment
summary: Raises the appointment score of a character for the title.
details: Runs on a title.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The character who gets the score.

fields.name: value
fields.text: How much to add.
fields.values: a number or a script value

fields.name: investor
fields.text: The character who made the investment.

label: Cohesion
summary: Changes the confederation's cohesion by the given amount.
details: Runs on a confederation. Vanilla uses negative numbers (-20, -100) to lower it.
